whatIsKnasty.title: What is Knasty Portal?
whatIsKnasty.content:
Knasty Portal is a comprehensive Sunday School Management System designed to streamline the administration and engagement of Sunday school programs. It provides tools for students to participate in activities, teachers to manage classes and attendance, parents to monitor their children's progress, and church administrators to oversee all aspects of the program.

The system is built with accessibility and internationalization in mind, supporting both English and Arabic with full RTL (Right-to-Left) support. It uses Next.js for a modern, responsive user interface and Supabase for secure database management and authentication.

features.title: Key Features
features.content:
Student Dashboard — View announcements, join trips and activities, manage store orders, and earn points through competitions

Class Management — Teachers can create and manage classes, track attendance, and communicate with students

Attendance Tracking — Automated attendance marking with historical records and reporting

Trips & Activities — Organize events with approval workflows, payment tracking, and attendance management

Store System — Sell items to students with ordering and inventory management

Gamification — Points, streaks, badges, and leaderboards to motivate student participation

Parent Portal — Parents can approve activities, monitor children's progress, and view announcements

Role-Based Access — Different interfaces and permissions for students, teachers, parents, and administrators

Bilingual Support — Full English and Arabic support with automatic RTL layout for Arabic

Rich Notifications — Real-time announcements and notifications to keep everyone informed

roles.title: User Roles
roles.content:
Student — Can view announcements, join activities and trips, use the store, and view their profile and points

Teacher — Can manage classes, take attendance, create announcements, and manage trips

Parent — Can monitor children, approve activities, view announcements, and manage store orders

Church Admin — Manages all aspects of the church including classes, users, students, attendance, and announcements

Diocese Admin — Oversees multiple churches, manages diocesan-level users and settings

Super Admin — Full system access including dioceses, roles, permissions, and system health monitoring

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.content:
1. Login — Visit the login page and enter your email or user code and password

2. Find Your Section — Based on your role, you'll have access to different sections of Knasty Portal

3. Navigate — Use the sidebar or menu to navigate to different areas

4. View Documentation — Use the Documentation link available on the login page or in your dashboard to learn more about specific features

5. Contact Support — If you encounter issues, reach out to your church or diocese administrator

If you don't have an account, contact your church or school administrator to create one.

dashboardOverview.title: Dashboard Overview
dashboardOverview.content:
The Student Dashboard is your main hub where you can see announcements, view your points and achievements, and access all your activities.

Key sections include:

Announcements — See the latest updates from teachers and administrators

My Points — View your current points balance and rank on the leaderboard

Upcoming Events — See trips and activities you can join

Quick Actions — Quick links to access store, activities, and trips

Your Profile — View and edit your personal information

trips.title: Trips
trips.content:
Trips are outings organized by your church or teachers. To join a trip:

1. Browse available trips on the Trips page

2. Click on a trip to view details, including date, location, cost, and what to bring

3. Click 'Join' to register for the trip

4. Wait for approval from the organizer

5. Once approved, you'll see the trip in your approved list

Your parent or guardian may need to approve your participation. After the trip, attendance may be recorded. You can view your trip history anytime.

store.title: Store
store.content:
The Store lets you purchase items. To buy items:

1. Browse available items on the Store page

2. Click on an item to see details and price

3. Click 'Add to Cart' to add it to your shopping cart

4. Review your cart and proceed to checkout

5. Select a payment method and complete your order

6. Track your order status in 'My Orders'

Your parent or guardian may need to approve certain orders. You'll receive notifications when your order status changes.

activities.title: Activities
activities.content:
Activities are skill-building or recreational programs offered by your church. To join:

1. Visit the Activities section

2. Browse and filter activities by category or date

3. Click on an activity to learn more about it

4. Click 'Register' to join

5. Your registration may require parent/guardian approval

Once registered, you'll receive updates about the activity schedule, location, and any requirements. Attending activities often earns you points toward the leaderboard!

competitions.title: Competitions
competitions.content:
Compete with other students in various challenges to earn points and badges:

1. View active competitions in the Competitions section

2. Understand the rules and scoring criteria

3. Submit your entries or scores as directed

4. Check the leaderboard to see how you rank

Winning competitions and participating consistently helps you climb the leaderboard and earn special badges. Friendly competition is encouraged!

spiritualNotes.title: Spiritual Notes
spiritualNotes.content:
Spiritual Notes allow you to record personal spiritual reflections and lessons learned during Sunday School.

To add a spiritual note:

1. Open the Spiritual Notes section

2. Click 'Add Note'

3. Write your reflection or lesson

4. Optionally add the date and any tags

5. Save your note

Your notes are private and visible only to you unless you choose to share them. Teachers may occasionally prompt you to write reflections on specific topics.

gamification.title: Gamification & Rewards
gamification.content:
Knasty Portal uses points, streaks, and badges to keep you motivated:

Points — Earned by attending classes, completing activities, winning competitions, and participating in events. Points accumulate in your account.

Streaks — Build streaks by attending class regularly. The longer your streak, the more points you earn!

Badges — Earn special badges by achieving milestones (first trip, 10 activities, 100 points, etc.)

Leaderboard — See where you rank among your peers based on points. Check your class leaderboard to compete with classmates.

Redeem Points — Depending on your church's settings, you may be able to redeem points for prizes or discounts.

profile.title: Your Profile
profile.content:
Your profile contains your personal information and achievements.

To view or edit your profile:

1. Click on your profile icon or name in the dashboard

2. View your personal information, avatar, and contact details

3. Edit your information by clicking 'Edit Profile'

4. Update your name, email, phone, or avatar

5. Save your changes

Your profile is visible to teachers and administrators. Make sure your contact information is up to date so you receive important notifications.

dashboardOverview.title: Dashboard Overview
dashboardOverview.content:
The Teacher Dashboard is your command center for managing classes, attendance, and student interactions.

Key sections include:

My Classes — View all classes you teach

Today's Attendance — Quickly see today's attendance status

Action Required — Items awaiting your attention

Upcoming Events — Trips and activities you're organizing

Announcements — Create and manage announcements to your students

Student Search — Quickly find and view specific students

classes.title: Classes
classes.content:
Manage your classes in the Classes section:

1. View all your classes with class name, grade, number of students, and last attendance date

2. Click on a class to view detailed information

3. See student roster and individual attendance records

4. Click 'Edit' to update class information like name, description, or schedule

5. Archive classes that are no longer active

Each class has its own student list, attendance records, and activity assignments. You can view individual student details, attendance history, and notes.

attendance.title: Attendance Marking
attendance.content:
Mark student attendance to track participation:

1. Go to your class and click 'Mark Attendance'

2. You'll see a list of all enrolled students

3. For each student, mark them as:
   - Present (attended)
   - Absent (did not attend)
   - Late (arrived after class started)
   - Excused (absent with valid reason)

4. Add notes if needed to explain absences

5. Click 'Save Attendance' to record

Attendance records are saved and can be viewed later. Regular attendance builds student streaks and points!

studentDrawer.title: Student Drawer
studentDrawer.content:
The Student Drawer gives you quick access to detailed student information:

1. From any class or student list, click on a student's name to open their drawer

2. View their:
   - Contact information
   - Current points and rank
   - Attendance history
   - Registered activities and trips
   - Personal notes

3. Add or update private notes about the student

4. View recent announcements sent to the student

This is a quick way to understand a student's engagement level without leaving your current page.

trips.title: Organizing & Managing Trips
trips.content:
You can create and manage trips:

1. Go to Trips and click 'Create Trip'

2. Enter trip details: name, date, location, description, cost, and capacity

3. Set approval workflow (does trip need student or parent approval?)

4. Add trip organizers and leaders

5. Publish the trip to make it available

Once students register:

1. Review pending registrations and approve/reject them

2. Track payment status for each participant

3. On the trip day, mark attendance

4. After the trip, record final attendance and points awarded

announcements.title: Creating Announcements
announcements.content:
Send announcements to your students:

1. Go to Announcements and click 'Create Announcement'

2. Choose your target audience (entire class or specific students)

3. Write your announcement title and message

4. Select when to send (now or schedule for later)

5. Choose notification method (notification, email, or both)

6. Review and publish

Announcements appear in the student dashboard and as notifications. Use announcements to share important dates, reminders, and updates about your class.

studentSearch.title: Student Search
studentSearch.content:
Quickly find students across all classes:

1. Click the Search icon or use the search bar

2. Type a student's name, email, or ID code

3. Results will show matching students

4. Click on a result to view the student's detailed profile

5. From the profile, you can view attendance, activities, and notes

This is useful when you need to find a student outside your regular classes or check on a specific student's information.

dashboardOverview.title: Dashboard Overview
dashboardOverview.content:
The Parent Dashboard is your control center for managing your children's Sunday School engagement. It provides real-time visibility into their activities, pending approvals, points, and achievements.

📋 Dashboard Layout:

🔹 Top Navigation Bar:
- Menu button (hamburger icon) on the left to open the sidebar
- Knasty logo in the center linking back to the main dashboard
- Child Selector dropdown in the center showing current child or "All Children"
- Notification bell icon showing total count of pending approvals + unread notifications
- Your profile avatar in the top right

🔹 Left Sidebar (tap menu button to open):
- Home section with Dashboard link
- My Children section listing all your children with their current points balance
- Actions section with:
  • Pending Approvals (shows red badge with count)
  • Notifications (shows red badge with unread count)
  • Announcements
- For My Children section with:
  • Store (tap to order items)
  • Orders (view order history)
  • Trips (view and register for trips)
  • Activities (view available activities)
- Account section with Profile, Settings, and Documentation links
- Logout button at the bottom

📸 Visual: After login, you see the navbar with your name, the Knasty logo, child selector with current points, notification bell, and your avatar.

💡 Tips:
- Use the Child Selector to switch between your children — all information updates instantly
- The red badges show urgent items needing your attention
- Tap your avatar to view or edit your profile
- Check notifications regularly to stay informed about your children's activities

childSelector.title: Child Selector
childSelector.content:
The Child Selector allows you to view information for different children and filter activities by child. It's located in the center of the top navigation bar.

📋 Child Selector Overview:

🔹 When Selecting a Single Child:
Step 1: Look at the top center of the screen — you'll see a dropdown showing your selected child's name, avatar, class, and current points balance.
Step 2: Click the dropdown to view all your children.
Step 3: Select a child from the list.
Step 4: The entire dashboard updates to show only that child's information (points, activities, pending approvals, etc.)
Step 5: The navbar dropdown now shows the selected child's details.

🔹 When Selecting "All Children":
Step 1: Click the Child Selector dropdown.
Step 2: Select "All Children" (shown with a blue users icon).
Step 3: The dashboard shows aggregated information for all your children.
Step 4: This view is useful for seeing a quick overview of all children's pending approvals.

📸 Visual: The Child Selector shows an avatar, child's name in large text, child's class name and points balance in smaller text below.

💡 Tips:
- Switch between children to check on each one's progress
- The child's current points balance is always displayed next to their name
- On pages like Store or Trips, when you tap "Store" or "Trips" from the sidebar with multiple children, a dialog appears asking you to select which child to shop or register for
- Each child can have different pending approvals, so check each one

childProfile.title: Your Child's Profile
childProfile.content:
The Child Profile page shows detailed information about your selected child's achievements, engagement, and progress in the Sunday School program.

📋 Accessing Child Profile:

🔹 From Dashboard:
Step 1: Open the sidebar (tap menu button).
Step 2: In the "My Children" section, tap your child's name.
Step 3: The page navigates to that child's profile showing their full details.

🔹 Profile Information Displayed:
Step 1: Child's avatar, name, and personal information at the top.
Step 2: Current class assignment with class name.
Step 3: Points & Rank section showing:
   - Current available points balance
   - Total points earned
   - Current rank on the leaderboard
Step 4: Badges & Achievements section:
   - Badges earned (e.g., "First Trip", "100 Points", "10 Activities")
   - Click a badge to see more details about how to earn it
Step 5: Attendance section showing:
   - Current attendance streak (e.g., "5 weeks attended")
   - Recent attendance records
   - Attendance rate as a percentage
Step 6: Activities & Trips section:
   - Upcoming activities your child is registered for
   - Completed activities and trips
   - Points earned from each

📸 Visual: The profile shows the child's avatar and name prominently at top, with cards below showing points balance (with star icon), current rank, earned badges, attendance streak, and activity history.

💡 Tips:
- The points balance shown includes only available points (redeemed points are deducted)
- Badges are achievements unlocked through participation
- Attendance streaks are built by attending every Sunday School class
- Check the profile regularly to see your child's progress and encourage continued participation

approvals.title: Approving Activities & Trips
approvals.content:
The Approvals page lets you review and approve or reject your child's requests to join trips and activities. This is an important responsibility as timely approvals ensure your child doesn't miss registration deadlines.

📋 Accessing Pending Approvals:

🔹 Method 1 - From Sidebar:
Step 1: Open the menu (tap hamburger icon).
Step 2: In the "Actions" section, tap "Pending Approvals".
Step 3: You'll see a red badge showing the number of pending items.
Step 4: The Approvals page loads showing all pending requests.

🔹 Method 2 - From Home:
Step 1: On the Dashboard, look for the "Pending Approvals" card.
Step 2: Tap to view all pending items.

📋 How to Approve a Request:

Step 1: Review the pending request details:
   - Child's name
   - Activity or Trip name
   - Type (Activity, Trip, or Overnight Trip)
   - Dates (start and end dates if applicable)
   - Location
   - Cost/Points required
   - Description of what it is
Step 2: Read the full details including what the activity involves.
Step 3: Click the green "Approve" button.
Step 4: A confirmation dialog appears — tap "Confirm" to approve.
Step 5: Your approval is recorded and the child is notified immediately.
Step 6: The request moves to the Approval History section.

📋 How to Reject a Request:

Step 1: Review the request details.
Step 2: If you decide not to approve, click the red "Reject" button.
Step 3: An optional reason dialog appears.
Step 4: Type a reason (e.g., "Conflict with family plans", "Not appropriate at this time").
Step 5: Click "Confirm" to reject.
Step 6: The child is notified of the rejection and the reason if you provided one.
Step 7: The request moves to the Approval History section.

📋 Approval History:

Step 1: Below pending approvals, you'll see "Approval History".
Step 2: This shows all previously approved and rejected requests.
Step 3: You can click any history item to view its details again.
Step 4: The status (Approved or Rejected) and decision date are shown.

📸 Visual: The Approvals page has two main sections — Pending (with "Approve" and "Reject" buttons) and History (showing past decisions with dates and status badges).

💡 Tips:
- Check Pending Approvals frequently — requests often have quick registration deadlines
- When you approve, the child's teacher is notified and they're registered automatically
- When you reject, give a reason so your child understands the decision
- Payment for trips is usually collected after approval, not before
- Some activities may require your approval before the child can register
- The red notification badge disappears once all pending approvals are reviewed

notifications.title: Managing Notifications
notifications.content:
Notifications keep you informed about your children's activities, approvals, and important updates. You can view and manage them in the Notifications section.

📋 Types of Notifications You'll Receive:

🔹 Activity-Related:
- New trips your child can register for
- New activities available for your child
- Activities your child is registered for (confirmations, reminders)
- Upcoming activity dates and deadlines

🔹 Approval-Related:
- New pending approval requests (when child tries to join something)
- Reminders about pending approvals requiring your action
- Approval decision confirmations

🔹 Attendance & Points:
- Attendance records (when attendance is marked)
- Badge achievements (when your child earns a new badge)
- Streak updates (when attendance streak is recorded)
- Points awarded notifications

🔹 Payment-Related:
- Payment reminders for trip costs
- Order confirmation notifications
- Order status updates (processing, ready for pickup, delivered)

🔹 Announcements:
- Important messages from teachers
- Church announcements
- General updates about the Sunday School program

📋 Accessing Notifications:

🔹 From the Bell Icon:
Step 1: Look at the top right of the screen.
Step 2: Tap the bell icon (notification button).
Step 3: If there's a number badge, that's your count of unread items.
Step 4: The Notifications page opens showing all recent notifications.

🔹 From the Sidebar:
Step 1: Open the menu (tap hamburger icon).
Step 2: In the "Actions" section, tap "Notifications".
Step 3: You'll see a red badge showing the unread count.
Step 4: The Notifications page loads.

📋 Viewing Notification Details:

Step 1: On the Notifications page, you'll see a list of notifications sorted by date (newest first).
Step 2: Each notification shows:
   - An icon (indicating the type: activity, approval, announcement, etc.)
   - The notification title and a brief preview
   - The date and time
   - If it's unread (highlighted or marked as unread)
Step 3: Click any notification to see full details.
Step 4: The notification details page shows the complete message and relevant information.
Step 5: You can tap related links (e.g., "View Activity", "View Approval") to navigate to the item.

📋 Marking Notifications as Read:

🔹 Mark One as Read:
Step 1: On the notification item, look for a read/unread icon (often a circle or dot).
Step 2: Click the icon or the notification itself to mark it as read.
Step 3: The highlight disappears and the unread badge count decreases.

🔹 Mark All as Read:
Step 1: On the Notifications page, look for a "Mark All as Read" button (usually at the top or in a menu).
Step 2: Tap the button.
Step 3: All notifications are marked as read at once.
Step 4: The bell icon badge disappears.

📋 Customizing Notification Preferences:

Step 1: Open the menu (tap hamburger icon).
Step 2: Tap "Settings" in the Account section.
Step 3: Find the "Notifications" settings area.
Step 4: For each notification type, choose:
   - On/Off to enable or disable
   - Delivery method: Email, In-App (push), or Both
Step 5: Save your preferences.
Step 6: Your settings take effect immediately.

📸 Visual: The Notifications page shows a chronological list of items with icons, titles, brief text, dates, and read/unread indicators. The bell icon in the top navbar shows a red number badge if there are unread items.

💡 Tips:
- The bell icon badge shows your total unread count (approvals + notifications combined)
- Marking notifications as read removes the highlight but doesn't delete them
- You can still access read notifications by scrolling down or using filters
- For urgent items (like approvals with deadlines), enable email notifications
- Customize settings to avoid notification overload while staying informed
- Check notifications regularly to stay updated on your child's activities

store.title: Ordering From the Store
store.content:
The Store is a key feature of the Sunday School program. Parents can order items for their children using the child's accumulated points. This comprehensive guide walks you through the entire ordering process.

📋 Accessing the Store:

🔹 Method 1 - From Sidebar:
Step 1: Open the menu (tap the hamburger icon on the top left).
Step 2: Scroll down to "For My Children" section.
Step 3: Tap "Store" (with shopping bag icon).
Step 4: If you have multiple children, a dialog appears asking "Select Child for Store".
Step 5: Choose which child you want to order for.
Step 6: The Store page loads showing available items for that child.

🔹 Method 2 - From Dashboard:
Step 1: Look for a "Store" card or link on your dashboard.
Step 2: Tap it to go directly to the Store.
Step 3: If multiple children, select the child you want to order for.

📋 Understanding Available Items:

Step 1: The Store displays items available for your child in a grid or list format.
Step 2: Each item shows:
   - Item image/picture
   - Item name
   - Price in points (e.g., "150 pts")
   - A brief description
   - Stock status (In Stock, Limited Stock, Out of Stock)
Step 3: Different items may have different pricing based on your child's tier:
   - Normal price (standard price for most children)
   - Discount prices may apply based on your child's status
Step 4: Items are curated by the church and may include:
   - Snacks and treats
   - Small prizes and rewards
   - School supplies
   - Spiritual books or materials
   - Gift items

📋 Viewing Item Details:

Step 1: Click or tap an item to see its full details.
Step 2: A detail view opens (or a modal/popup appears) showing:
   - Large item image
   - Item name and description
   - Price in points
   - Availability status
   - Any special notes (e.g., "Limited to 5 per order")
Step 3: If you want to purchase, you'll see the "Add to Cart" button.
Step 4: If you don't want this item, tap back or close to return to the store.

📋 Adding Items to Cart:

Step 1: While viewing an item or on the main store page, tap or click "Add to Cart".
Step 2: If this is the first time, a cart is created.
Step 3: A success message appears: "Item added to cart" (or similar).
Step 4: The item is now in your cart.
Step 5: To add more of the same item, increase the quantity (look for + button).
Step 6: You can add multiple different items to the same cart.
Step 7: At the top or bottom of the page, you'll see a "Cart" button/link showing the number of items (e.g., "Cart (3)").

📋 Reviewing Your Cart:

Step 1: Look for the shopping cart icon or "View Cart" button.
Step 2: Tap it to see your full cart contents.
Step 3: The cart displays:
   - Each item added with its name, quantity, and price per item
   - Subtotal for each item (quantity × points per item)
   - Total points for the entire order
   - Your child's current available points balance
   - A comparison showing "You have X points, this order costs Y points"
Step 4: You can:
   - Increase or decrease quantity with + and - buttons
   - Remove an item by clicking the trash/delete icon
   - Continue shopping by clicking "Continue Shopping"
Step 5: Verify all items and quantities are correct before checkout.

📋 Checking Your Child's Points Balance:

Step 1: Before placing an order, always check the available points balance.
Step 2: This is shown:
   - In the cart review page ("Available Points: X")
   - In the top navbar Child Selector (points shown next to child's name)
   - In the child's profile
Step 3: If the order total exceeds available points:
   - The "Proceed to Checkout" button may be disabled
   - An error message displays
   - You cannot place the order with insufficient points
Step 4: Points are earned through:
   - Attendance (attending Sunday School classes)
   - Completing activities
   - Winning competitions
   - Special achievements

📋 Placing the Order (Checkout):

Step 1: Review your cart one final time.
Step 2: Tap the "Proceed to Checkout" or "Place Order" button.
Step 3: A confirmation dialog or page appears showing:
   - All items in the order
   - Total points that will be deducted
   - Your child's name (for whom the order is being placed)
   - Optional order notes field (for special requests or instructions)
Step 4: Optionally, add notes (e.g., "Please include extra napkins").
Step 5: Review the information one more time.
Step 6: Tap "Confirm Order" or "Complete Order".
Step 7: An order confirmation message appears with an order number.
Step 8: Your child's available points are immediately deducted from their balance.
Step 9: The cart is cleared.

📋 Order Status & Tracking:

Step 1: After placing an order, you can track its status.
Step 2: Go to "Orders" (tap menu → "Orders" or find Orders link).
Step 3: The Orders page shows all orders for your selected child.
Step 4: Each order displays:
   - Order date and order ID
   - Items in the order
   - Order status (e.g., "Pending", "Being Prepared", "Ready for Pickup", "Completed")
   - Total points charged
Step 5: Click an order to see detailed information:
   - Individual items with quantities and prices
   - Order notes
   - Status history and timestamps
   - Pickup or delivery information (if applicable)
Step 6: Most orders are fulfilled within 2-3 business days.
Step 7: You'll receive a notification when the status changes.

📋 Common Store Scenarios:

🔹 What if I don't have enough points?
- You cannot place an order that exceeds your child's available points
- Consider saving up points for the next purchase
- Encourage your child to attend classes and activities to earn more points

🔹 Can I edit an order after placing it?
- Once an order is placed and confirmed, you generally cannot edit it
- Contact the church admin if you need to cancel or modify a very recent order

🔹 What if an item is out of stock?
- Out of stock items won't appear in the store, or may be grayed out
- Check back later when new inventory arrives
- Some items may have a "Notify Me" option to alert you when back in stock

🔹 Are there pricing tiers?
- Some children may have different prices based on their tier (Normal, Mastor, Botl)
- Pricing is automatically applied based on your child's profile
- Contact your church if you have questions about pricing

🔹 How do I check my child's order history?
- Go to Orders (via sidebar "Orders" link or from Store page)
- View all past and current orders
- See what items your child has purchased over time

📸 Visual: The Store page shows a grid of colorful product cards with images, names, prices in points, and "Add to Cart" buttons. The Cart view shows a list of selected items with quantity controls and a total points calculation. The Orders page displays a chronological list of past orders with status badges and order details.

💡 Tips:
- Check the Store regularly for new items and seasonal offerings
- Help your child pick items they'll enjoy and find valuable
- Use store orders as a reward for good attendance and behavior
- Set a budget and teach your child about point management
- Point balances reset based on your church's policy (typically annually)
- Encourage your child to earn points through participation rather than large one-time purchases
- Orders typically don't involve parent payment — they use the child's earned points
- Most churches allow you to see all available items without age restrictions, but some items may be limited by age or class

trips.title: Managing Trip Participation
trips.content:
Trips are organized outings for the Sunday School students. As a parent, you can browse available trips, register your child, approve participation, and track payments. This guide walks through the complete trip workflow.

📋 Accessing the Trips Section:

🔹 Method 1 - From Sidebar:
Step 1: Open the menu (tap hamburger icon).
Step 2: In "For My Children" section, tap "Trips" (with bus icon).
Step 3: If you have multiple children, a dialog asks "Select Child for Trips".
Step 4: Choose which child you want to register for trips.
Step 5: The Trips page loads showing available trips for that child.

🔹 Method 2 - From Dashboard:
Step 1: Look for a "Trips" card or link.
Step 2: Tap it to navigate to Trips.
Step 3: Select a child if prompted.

📋 Browsing Available Trips:

Step 1: The Trips page displays all available trips your child can join.
Step 2: Each trip card shows:
   - Trip name/title (e.g., "Zoo Outing", "Hiking Adventure")
   - Date(s) and time
   - Location
   - Brief description
   - Cost in points (if trip uses points) or currency amount (if paid)
   - Number of spots remaining / total capacity
Step 3: Trips may be labeled by type:
   - Day Trip (e.g., "Saturday 2-5 PM")
   - Overnight Trip (e.g., "Friday evening - Sunday morning")
   - Multi-day Trip
Step 4: Some trips may show:
   - Age/grade requirements (e.g., "Ages 8-12")
   - What to bring (e.g., "Bring swimsuit and towel")
   - Special notes (e.g., "Parental supervision not required")
Step 5: Use filters to narrow down trips by:
   - Date range
   - Type (day trip, overnight, etc.)
   - Location
Step 6: Search for specific trips by name or keyword.

📋 Viewing Trip Details:

Step 1: Tap a trip card to see full details.
Step 2: The trip detail page shows:
   - Large trip name and cover image
   - Full description of the activity
   - Dates and times (start and end)
   - Location and address
   - Cost/Points required
   - Capacity and spots remaining
   - What to bring (packing list)
   - Pickup and dropoff details
   - Contact information for the trip organizer
   - Any special requirements or notes
   - Approval requirements (Does it need parent approval? Teacher approval?)
Step 3: Read through all details carefully to understand what the trip involves.
Step 4: If interested, you'll see a "Register" button.
Step 5: If you want to ask questions, look for a "Contact Organizer" option.

📋 Registering Your Child for a Trip:

Step 1: After reviewing trip details, tap the "Register" button.
Step 2: A confirmation dialog appears showing:
   - Child's name
   - Trip name and date
   - Total cost/points required
   - Confirmation checkbox ("I understand the trip details...")
Step 3: Review the information one more time.
Step 4: Check the confirmation checkbox.
Step 5: Tap "Confirm Registration".
Step 6: A success message appears: "Your child has been registered for [Trip Name]".
Step 7: The registration status changes to "Pending Parent Approval" or "Confirmed" depending on the trip's approval workflow.

📋 Approval Workflow (Parent Approval):

Step 1: After your child registers, a pending approval appears on your dashboard.
Step 2: You'll receive a notification about the pending approval.
Step 3: Go to "Pending Approvals" (sidebar → Approvals).
Step 4: Find the trip approval request.
Step 5: Review the trip details again:
   - Trip name, dates, location
   - Cost and what's required
   - What to bring
Step 6: Decide to approve or reject:
   - Tap "Approve" to allow your child to go
   - Tap "Reject" to decline and optionally provide a reason
Step 7: Once approved:
   - Your child's registration is confirmed
   - They receive a confirmation notification
   - Payment (if required) becomes due
Step 8: If rejected:
   - Your child is notified of the rejection
   - The registration is canceled
   - Points are not charged (if using points)

📋 Payment & Cost Information:

🔹 Point-Based Trips:
Step 1: If the trip costs points (e.g., "150 pts"):
   - The points are deducted from your child's available balance upon approval
   - You need to ensure your child has enough points
   - If insufficient points, you cannot approve the trip
Step 2: Your child's points balance is shown in the trip details.
Step 3: After approval, points are immediately charged.

🔹 Cash-Based Trips:
Step 1: If the trip requires payment (e.g., "$25.00"):
   - Payment details are provided in the trip information
   - The church may collect payment via:
     • School/church office payment (in-person)
     • Online payment link
     • Check or cash
Step 2: Check the trip details for specific payment instructions.
Step 3: Payment deadline is typically listed (e.g., "Must be paid by December 15").
Step 4: You'll receive reminders for upcoming payment deadlines.

📋 Tracking Trip Registration Status:

Step 1: Go to Trips page to see all your child's trips.
Step 2: Filter by status to see:
   - Upcoming trips (approved and confirmed)
   - Pending approval trips (waiting for your decision)
   - Past trips (completed)
Step 3: Each trip shows:
   - Current status badge (Pending Approval, Confirmed, Completed)
   - Days until trip countdown
   - Payment status (Paid, Due, Pending)
Step 4: Tap a trip to see full status details.
Step 5: Some trips may show "Payment Reminder" if payment is due soon.

📋 Before the Trip:

Step 1: As the trip date approaches, you'll receive reminders.
Step 2: Review what your child needs to bring.
Step 3: Prepare the packing list items.
Step 4: Confirm payment if required.
Step 5: Note the pickup and dropoff times.
Step 6: Ensure your child has any required medications or documents.

📋 Canceling a Trip Registration:

Step 1: If you need to cancel your child's trip registration:
Step 2: Go to the specific trip on the Trips page.
Step 3: Look for a "Cancel Registration" or "Withdraw" button.
Step 4: A confirmation dialog appears asking why (optional reason).
Step 5: Tap "Confirm Cancellation".
Step 6: The registration is canceled.
Step 7: If points were charged, they may be refunded (check church policy).
Step 8: The trip organizer is notified of the cancellation.

📋 After the Trip:

Step 1: Once the trip is completed, the status changes to "Completed".
Step 2: You'll receive an after-trip report showing:
   - Attendance (whether your child attended)
   - Photos from the trip (if shared)
   - Feedback or comments from trip organizers
Step 3: Your child may earn points for trip attendance.
Step 4: The trip moves to the "Past Trips" section.
Step 5: You can still view all trip details and attendance records anytime.

📸 Visual: The Trips page shows a list or grid of trip cards with dates, locations, costs, and registration buttons. Trip details page shows a full description with dates, location, what to bring, cost, and Approve/Reject buttons when in pending approval. The registration status is clearly marked with color-coded badges (yellow for pending, green for approved, gray for completed).

💡 Tips:
- Review trips well in advance — some have registration deadlines
- Check the "What to Bring" list before each trip
- Keep an eye on payment deadlines to avoid last-minute rush
- Read the full trip description to understand what's involved
- Approve trips promptly when possible — delays may mean missing the trip
- Contact the trip organizer if you have questions or concerns
- Ask your child what they enjoyed about past trips
- Trips are great opportunities for your child to make friends and have new experiences
- Points from trips go toward leaderboard ranking and store purchases

activities.title: Monitoring Activities & Competitions
activities.content:
Activities are skill-building programs that your children can participate in to earn points and develop new interests. The Activities section lets you browse available programs, monitor your child's participation, and track their progress. This guide covers all aspects of the Activities feature.

📋 Accessing the Activities Section:

🔹 Method 1 - From Sidebar:
Step 1: Open the menu (tap hamburger icon).
Step 2: In "For My Children" section, tap "Activities" (with activity icon).
Step 3: If you have multiple children, a dialog asks "Select Child for Activities".
Step 4: Choose which child you want to view activities for.
Step 5: The Activities page loads.

🔹 Method 2 - From Dashboard:
Step 1: Look for an "Activities" card or link.
Step 2: Tap it to navigate to Activities.
Step 3: Select a child if prompted.

📋 Understanding Activity Types:

There are several types of activities your child can participate in:

🔹 Skill-Building Activities:
- Programs that teach new skills (e.g., art, music, sports, coding)
- Usually meet on a regular schedule
- May require registration or application
- Points awarded for completion or attendance

🔹 Competitions:
- Contests where children compete for prizes and points
- Examples: spelling bee, math competition, art contest
- May be ongoing or one-time events
- Points awarded based on placement or participation

🔹 Readings:
- Structured reading programs or book clubs
- May include discussion or comprehension tests
- Points awarded for completion

🔹 Spiritual Notes / Reflections:
- Personal reflection activities
- Children write about spiritual lessons or Sunday school topics
- Points awarded for thoughtful submissions

📋 Browsing Available Activities:

Step 1: The Activities page displays all available activities.
Step 2: Each activity shows:
   - Activity name and type (Skill-Building, Competition, Reading, etc.)
   - Brief description
   - Schedule/dates
   - Points value (how many points can be earned)
   - Current status (Open for Registration, Full, Closed, Ongoing)
   - Number of participants
Step 3: Filter activities by:
   - Type (Skill-Building, Competition, Reading, etc.)
   - Points value
   - Date range
   - Status
Step 4: Search for specific activities by name or keyword.
Step 5: View activities your child is:
   - Already registered for
   - Completed
   - Can still register for

📋 Viewing Activity Details:

Step 1: Tap an activity to see full details.
Step 2: The activity detail page shows:
   - Activity name and type
   - Full description of what it involves
   - Schedule (dates, times, frequency)
   - Location (if in-person) or format (online, hybrid)
   - Points value and how points are earned
   - Eligibility requirements (age, grade, skill level)
   - Registration deadline
   - Capacity and current enrollment
   - Instructor or leader name
   - Required materials or preparation
   - How completion is tracked
Step 3: Read all details carefully.
Step 4: Note the registration deadline — don't miss it!
Step 5: If interested, you'll see a "Register" button.
Step 6: If you have questions, look for a "Contact" or "Message Organizer" option.

📋 Registering Your Child for an Activity:

Step 1: After reviewing, tap "Register" button.
Step 2: A confirmation dialog appears showing:
   - Child's name
   - Activity name
   - Schedule and commitment
   - Points available
   - Any special notes
Step 3: Review once more.
Step 4: Tap "Confirm Registration".
Step 5: A success message confirms registration.
Step 6: The activity now appears in "My Activities" or "Registered Activities" section.
Step 7: You'll receive a notification confirming registration.

📋 Monitoring Your Child's Progress:

🔹 View Registered Activities:
Step 1: Go to Activities page and filter by "Registered" or "My Activities".
Step 2: See all activities your child is currently enrolled in.
Step 3: For each activity, see:
   - Current status (In Progress, Completed, etc.)
   - Dates and schedule
   - Attendance record (if applicable)
   - Points earned so far

🔹 Track Completion:
Step 1: Click into an ongoing activity to see details.
Step 2: View completion progress (e.g., "Attended 4 out of 6 sessions").
Step 3: See any assignments or required components.
Step 4: Check if all components are completed.
Step 5: Once all requirements are met, the activity status changes to "Completed".

🔹 View Points Earned:
Step 1: After your child completes an activity, points are awarded.
Step 2: The activity detail shows points earned.
Step 3: Points are added to your child's total balance.
Step 4: You'll receive a notification when points are awarded.
Step 5: Verify the points in your child's profile (points balance increases).

📋 Different Activity Tracking Methods:

🔹 Attendance-Based Activities:
- Points awarded for showing up and participating
- Attendance is marked by the activity leader
- You see attendance records in the activity details
- Completion occurs after all sessions are attended

🔹 Submission-Based Activities (Readings, Spiritual Notes):
- Your child submits work (written reflections, completed reading responses)
- You may not see the full submission, but the status shows "Submitted"
- Instructor reviews and marks as complete
- Points awarded upon approval

🔹 Competition-Based Activities:
- Your child participates in the competition event
- Results are recorded (placement, score, time, etc.)
- Points awarded based on performance
- Leaderboard may show rankings

🔹 Goal-Based Activities:
- Your child works toward a goal (e.g., "Read 5 books", "Practice 10 times")
- Progress is tracked (e.g., "2 out of 5 books completed")
- Once goal is reached, points are awarded

📋 Understanding Points from Activities:

Step 1: Different activities award different points based on:
   - Difficulty level
   - Time commitment
   - Type of activity
   - Completion quality
Step 2: Points are earned by:
   - Completing the activity successfully
   - Attending all sessions
   - Achieving high marks/scores
   - Timely submission of work
Step 3: Points are added to your child's available balance immediately upon completion.
Step 4: Your child can use these points in the Store to purchase items.
Step 5: Points also count toward leaderboard rankings.

📋 Viewing Completed Activities:

Step 1: Filter activities by "Completed" or "Past Activities".
Step 2: See all activities your child has finished.
Step 3: For each completed activity, view:
   - Completion date
   - Points earned
   - Feedback or completion notes
   - Any certificates or achievements
Step 4: This shows your child's overall engagement and progress over time.

📋 Getting Reminders & Updates:

Step 1: You'll receive notifications about:
   - Upcoming activity registration deadlines
   - New activities your child might enjoy
   - When your child completes an activity
   - Points awarded notifications
   - Activity schedule reminders
Step 2: Enable activity notifications in Settings if you want more frequent updates.
Step 3: Activities with upcoming deadlines may show a countdown timer.

📋 Canceling Activity Registration:

Step 1: If your child needs to withdraw from an activity:
Step 2: Go to the activity on the Activities page.
Step 3: Look for a "Withdraw" or "Cancel Registration" button.
Step 4: A confirmation dialog appears.
Step 5: Optionally provide a reason.
Step 6: Tap "Confirm Cancellation".
Step 7: Your child is withdrawn from the activity.
Step 8: If points were already awarded, they may not be refunded (check church policy).
Step 9: The activity organizer is notified.

📈 Using Activities to Build Skills & Engagement:

💡 Tips:
- Encourage your child to try new activities and develop diverse skills
- Look at activities aligned with your child's interests
- Remind your child about registration deadlines
- Celebrate activity completions and points earned
- Use activities as motivation for good behavior and attendance
- Review completed activities to understand your child's progress
- Activities help your child make friends with classmates
- Points from activities can be used in the Store for rewards
- Some activities may be prerequisites for other programs
- Regular activity participation boosts leaderboard ranking
- Activities complement classroom learning with hands-on skills

📸 Visual: The Activities page shows a grid or list of activity cards with names, types, schedules, points values, and registration status badges. Activity details show a full description with enrollment options. The "My Activities" section shows registered and completed activities with progress indicators (progress bars, "In Progress" badges, "Completed" badges).

🎬 Expected Workflow:
1. Browse available activities on the Activities page
2. Click an activity to read full details
3. Register your child if interested
4. Receive confirmation and notifications
5. Child participates in activity
6. Upon completion, points are awarded
7. Check progress on Activities page
8. View total earned points in child's profile
9. Use points in the Store when ready

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.content:
Authentication is handled through Supabase Auth.

Server Actions (Client to Server):
- Login: Use the loginAction from the login page
- Logout: Use signOut from @/lib/auth
- Password Reset: Available on login page

API Routes (Direct HTTP):
- POST /api/auth/login — Login with credentials
- POST /api/auth/logout — Logout current session
- POST /api/auth/refresh — Refresh session token

All requests include auth via Supabase session cookies. No additional API keys needed for authenticated users.

Example:
```
const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({
  email: 'user@example.com',
  password: 'password'
})
```

Server Actions use the requireAuth() guard to ensure user is authenticated before executing.

endpoints.title: REST API Endpoints
endpoints.content:
Key API endpoints available:

Admin Endpoints:
- POST /api/admin/create-user — Create new user (requires admin)
- GET /api/admin/users — List users (requires admin)
- PUT /api/admin/users/:id — Update user (requires admin)
- DELETE /api/admin/users/:id — Delete user (requires admin)

Student Endpoints:
- GET /api/students/me — Get current student profile
- PUT /api/students/:id — Update student profile
- GET /api/students/:id/activities — List student activities
- GET /api/students/:id/trips — List student trips

Teacher Endpoints:
- GET /api/teachers/me — Get teacher profile
- POST /api/attendance/mark — Record attendance
- GET /api/classes/:id/students — List class students

Parent Endpoints:
- GET /api/parents/me — Get parent profile
- GET /api/parents/children — List parent's children

All endpoints require proper authentication and return JSON responses.

serverActions.title: Server Actions
serverActions.content:
Server Actions are functions that run on the server, called from client components:

Auth Guards Required:
- requireAuth() — Any authenticated user
- requireStaff() — Teachers and admins
- requireAdmin() — Admin roles only

Example Server Action:
```
'use server'
import { requireAuth } from '@/lib/auth-guard'

export async function updateProfile(data: ProfileData) {
  await requireAuth()  // Must be authenticated
  // Process update
  return result
}
```

Common Server Actions:
- loginAction(email, password) — Login
- signOut() — Logout
- updateProfile(data) — Update user profile
- markAttendance(studentId, status) — Record attendance
- createAnnouncement(data) — Create announcement
- registerForTrip(tripId) — Register for trip

Always include auth guards at the start of every server action.

errorHandling.title: Error Handling
errorHandling.content:
API responses use a consistent error format:

Success Response:
```
{
  success: true,
  data: { /* response data */ }
}
```

Error Response:
```
{
  success: false,
  error: 'Error message describing the issue'
}
```

Common Error Codes:
- 400 Bad Request — Invalid input
- 401 Unauthorized — Not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden — Not authorized (permission denied)
- 404 Not Found — Resource not found
- 409 Conflict — Duplicate record or conflict
- 422 Unprocessable — Validation failed
- 429 Too Many Requests — Rate limit exceeded
- 500 Internal Server Error — Server error

Always check the success flag and error message in responses. Display user-friendly error messages in the UI.

rateLimiting.title: Rate Limiting
rateLimiting.content:
The API implements rate limiting on sensitive endpoints:

Login Endpoint:
- Limit: 5 attempts per minute per IP
- Exceeding: Returns 429 status

Create User Endpoint:
- Limit: 10 creates per minute per user
- Exceeding: Returns 429 status

General API Endpoints:
- Limit: 100 requests per minute per user

When rate limited, the response includes:
```
{
  success: false,
  error: 'Too many requests. Please try again in X seconds.',
  retryAfter: 60
}
```

Implementation uses PostgreSQL-backed rate limiting for accuracy and persistence. Always implement exponential backoff when retrying rate-limited requests.

architecture.title: System Architecture
architecture.content:
Knasty Portal uses a modern Next.js architecture:

Frontend:
- Next.js 16 with App Router
- React for UI components
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- shadcn/ui for reusable components
- Zustand for state management

Backend:
- Next.js API routes and Server Actions
- Supabase for authentication and database
- PostgreSQL for data persistence
- Row Level Security (RLS) for data access control

Internationalization:
- next-intl for EN/AR support
- RTL-aware CSS (logical properties)
- Server-side and client-side translation

Security:
- OAuth/JWT via Supabase Auth
- CSRF protection on mutations
- Rate limiting on sensitive endpoints
- Content Security Policy (CSP)
- Input validation with Zod schemas

The architecture separates concerns: frontend handles UI, server actions handle business logic, and Supabase handles persistence and auth.

security.title: Security Implementation
security.content:
Security is built into every layer:

Authentication:
- Supabase Auth with session management
- Password hashing and bcrypt
- Email verification

Authorization:
- Role-based access control (RBAC)
- Auth guards on all server actions and API routes
- Role hierarchy enforcement

Data Protection:
- Row Level Security (RLS) on all tables
- Encrypted sensitive fields
- No sensitive data in logs

Input Validation:
- Zod schemas on all API inputs
- HTML sanitization before storage
- XSS prevention through DomPurify

Network Security:
- HTTPS only (enforced)
- CSRF tokens on mutations
- Secure cookies (SameSite, HttpOnly)
- Content Security Policy

Audit & Monitoring:
- Audit logs for all sensitive actions
- Failed login tracking
- Regular security scans
- Rate limiting to prevent abuse

Always assume user input is untrusted. Validate, sanitize, and escape all data.

database.title: Database Structure
database.content:
The database uses PostgreSQL with Supabase:

Core Tables:
- users — User accounts with roles
- profiles — Extended user information
- dioceses — Diocesan entities
- churches — Church entities
- classes — Class enrollments
- students — Student records
- attendance — Attendance logs
- activities — Activity definitions
- activity_registrations — Student activity signups
- trips — Trip definitions
- trip_registrations — Student trip signups
- store_items — Store inventory
- orders — Student orders
- points — Student point balances
- announcements — System announcements
- audit_logs — Activity logs

Migrations:
- Located in supabase/migrations/
- Numbered sequentially (00, 01, 02...)
- Include RLS policies
- Idempotent and reversible

Best Practices:
- Use explicit column selection (no SELECT *)
- Implement RLS on all new tables
- Add audit triggers for sensitive tables
- Use migrations for schema changes
- Test migrations before deploying

View CLAUDE.md for the full migration guide and database conventions.

permissions.title: Permission System
permissions.content:
Permissions control what users can do:

Role Hierarchy:
- Student (lowest)
- Parent
- Teacher
- Church Admin
- Diocese Admin
- Super Admin (highest)

Permission Checks:
- requireAuth() — Any logged-in user
- requireStaff() — Teachers and admins
- requireParent() — Parents only
- requireAdmin() — Admin roles (church admin and up)

Custom Permissions:
Use the PermissionsContext for fine-grained checks:
```
const { hasPermission } = usePermissions()
if (hasPermission('classes.edit')) {
  // Show edit button
}
```

Permission Scope:
- Role-level (all users with role can do action)
- Church-level (only church admin and above)
- Record-level (RLS on database)

Implement principle of least privilege: users get minimum permissions needed for their role.

internationalization.title: Internationalization (i18n)
internationalization.content:
The system supports English and Arabic with full RTL support:

Translation Files:
- messages/en.json — English translations
- messages/ar.json — Arabic translations
- Keys must match exactly between files

Server Components:
```
const t = await getTranslations('namespace')
const text = t('key.subkey')
```

Client Components:
```
const t = useTranslations('namespace')
const text = t('key.subkey')
```

CSS for RTL:
- Use ps-* / pe-* (padding start/end) instead of pl-* / pr-*
- Use ms-* / me-* (margin start/end) instead of ml-* / mr-*
- Use text-start / text-end instead of text-left / text-right
- Use border-s / border-e instead of border-l / border-r

When adding features:
1. Add English text to messages/en.json
2. Add matching Arabic translation to messages/ar.json
3. Use getTranslations() or useTranslations() in components
4. Run npm run check:i18n to verify parity

Always maintain key parity between English and Arabic.

codingConventions.title: Coding Conventions
codingConventions.content:
Follow these conventions for consistency:

File Naming:
- Pages: page.tsx
- Layouts: layout.tsx
- Client components: ComponentName.tsx (use 'use client')
- Server components: No special suffix
- API routes: route.ts

Component Structure:
- Props interface at top
- Component function with JSDoc
- Return single root element
- Use destructuring for props

Server Actions:
```
'use server'
import { requireAuth } from '@/lib/auth-guard'

export async function actionName(param: Type) {
  await requireAuth()  // FIRST LINE
  // Implementation
}
```

Error Handling:
- Use structured logger (not console.log)
- Return consistent error format
- Log all errors for debugging
- Show user-friendly error messages

Testing:
- Unit tests for utilities
- Integration tests for auth flows
- E2E tests for critical paths
- Security tests for auth/CSRF

Documentation:
- JSDoc comments on public functions
- Inline comments for complex logic
- README for new features

See CLAUDE.md for the complete development guide.

testing.title: Testing Guide
testing.content:
The project uses Vitest for unit tests and Playwright for E2E:

Test Commands:
- npm run test — Run all tests
- npm run test:unit — Unit tests only
- npm run test:integration — Integration tests
- npm run test:e2e — End-to-end tests
- npm run test:security — Security tests
- npm run test:a11y — Accessibility tests

Unit Tests (Vitest):
- Located in __tests__ directories
- Test pure functions and utilities
- Mock external dependencies
- Aim for 80%+ coverage

Integration Tests:
- Test auth flows and guards
- Test database queries
- Test permission checks
- Use test Supabase instance

E2E Tests (Playwright):
- Test user workflows
- Test critical features
- Run against staging/production
- Validate UI and interactions

Writing Tests:
```
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'

describe('myFunction', () => {
  it('should return correct value', () => {
    const result = myFunction(input)
    expect(result).toBe(expected)
  })
})
```

Before pushing code:
1. Run npm run test
2. Ensure all tests pass
3. Check code coverage
4. Review test output for failures

Maintain test suite as code evolves.
